text:
elaine: Heads-up, after the nightly build we started seeing a 20-30% p95 regression on FP8 paths for 8k context tests. Wasn’t present on yesterday's canary.

raj: ugh. which config? dedicated pool or hosted?

elaine: dedicated GPU pool, prod-sim job `perf/inference/8k/fp8` on a Hopper-like AMI. Baseline p95 ~42ms, now ~56ms.

marta: any change in batching heuristics or KV cache behavior? that can blow up when batch sizes slide.

elaine: I checked: batching heuristics in runtime unchanged. KV hit rate dropped from 98% to 86% for the test trace — most misses are at prefix sizes ~1-3k tokens.

boris: interesting. I pulled `perf top` on a repro run. Top stacks point to CUTLASS fallback paths and a lot more time in `dispatch_kernel` and `kv_cache::lookup` overhead. snippet:```
# perf top -p <pid>
  22.4% dispatch_kernel
  18.7% cutlass_fallback_gemm
  11.2% kv_cache::lookup
  6.5% kernel_launch_overhead
```

elaine: the build metadata shows a new arch-detect macro toggled in the nightly: `-DFORCE_CUTLASS_FALLBACK=auto_probe_arch`. suspect detection flip caused us to choose CUTLASS fallback kernels even though optimized FP8 kernels exist for this arch.

raj: why would that affect KV hit rate though?

elaine: hypothesis: dispatch latency up -> longer per-request tail -> batching windows shrink (we use time-based batching). When dispatch stalls, small requests are flushed less efficiently -> batches are smaller -> KV cache lookup patterns change and we see more misses because cached KV windows are less amortized.

marta: makes sense. smaller per-batch token count => more KV cache churn. Also CUTLASS fallback kernels may have different internal tensor alignment causing extra memcpys.

build-bot: Build 2026-03-15-23 triggered by commit 4f3b2e: `runtime: arch probe adjust for new CUDA kernels`

boris: I repro'd locally by toggling the macro off and running the same trace: p95 back to 44ms, KV hit rate back to 97.8%. So two correlated signals: arch probe -> fallback kernels -> latency -> smaller batches -> KV hit rate drop.

raj: what's the immediate mitigation? revert the macro? force CUTLASS off? toggle Triton kernels?

elaine: quick rollback of that build flag in nightly should restore. Longer-term we need: 1) safer arch-probing that verifies kernel perf delta before selecting fallback; 2) make batching heuristics robust to transient dispatch increases (grow time-window slightly or min-batch tokens); 3) better instrumentation to correlate kernel selection with KV hit telemetry.

marta: I'll open a small RFC for a safer probe: probe in a canary subset (1% of requests) and compare p95 and token throughput; only flip when delta < 5%. Also add a `kv_hit_rate` metric to the kernel selection dashboard.

boris: filing PR to revert the nightly compile flag now: PR #4829. Patch: change `-DFORCE_CUTLASS_FALLBACK=auto_probe_arch` -> `-DFORCE_CUTLASS_FALLBACK=disabled` in CI matrix.

elaine: thanks. I'll run a restored-build perf run after CI merges, and post numbers here. Also need a follow-up test: run long trace with Triton kernels explicitly enabled in the same build to compare.

marta: noted — I'll add a small test harness to the perf job to record: kernel_choice, batch_size_distribution, kv_hit_rate, p95. That should make future triage faster.

raj: are there any customers likely affected right now?

elaine: only internal prod-sim jobs and one dedicated customer using the new AMI. ops already rolled a patch VM to them; support pinged the account.

boris: also discovered a minor memcpy hotspot in `cutlass_fallback_gemm` when sequence length > 4096, opened issue #621. Might be separate but worth keeping an eye on.

elaine: summary: revert nightly flag (PR #4829), add canary probe + metrics RFC (marta), expand perf harness (marta/elaine), follow-up memcopy issue (boris). I'll update when CI + restored perf run complete. :thumbsup:
